# Meet Ollie 🦦

> *“Hey there, my dear friends!"* I’m **Ollie the Otter** , a curious river-explorer and data‑scientist‑in‑training. One morning while gliding along my favorite stream, I spotted a dairy barn where **hundreds of cows** were visiting automatic feeders and drinkers. The beeping RFID readers and steady munch-munch-munching created a beautiful data symphony!
>
> Each night, back at my mossy den, I curl up with my otter‑sized laptop and learn about R. The friendly farmers have shared their raw visit logs, so I can uncover the hidden tales behind my cow friends. I’m fascinated by how **every single cow writes its own story in the data**—and tonight we’re going to read their stories together using the **`moo4feed`** package. Ready to splash in? Let's go!

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("comics/data_cleaning.jpg")

```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Why Clean Your Data? 🧹

Raw data from automatic feeders is like my muddy riverbank - full of treasures but also plenty of muck! You'll find weird timestamps, strange visit records, and inconsistent file names. Cleaning transforms this mess into a crystal-clear stream perfect for analysis!

## 2. Gather Your Tools 🧰

```{r setup-packages}
library(moo4feed)   # 🐮 Your cow data helper!
```

Good news! `moo4feed` comes with sample files from friendly farmers, so you can follow along without your own data. Or edit the code to read in your own data when you're ready!

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. Where Are Your Files? 📂

```{r paths}
# 📝 USING YOUR OWN DATA? Edit this line: ---------------------------------
# extdata_path <- "/path/to/my/raw/files"  # ← your folder goes here

# JUST TRYING THE DEMO? No changes needed below: --------------------------
extdata_path <- system.file("extdata", package = "moo4feed")
```

### Feeders and drinkers in different folders?

No problem! Create two separate paths instead:

```{r echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
extdata_path_f <- "/path/to/feeder/files"    # 🐄 For feed data
extdata_path_w <- "/path/to/drinker/files"   # 🚰 For water data
```

Then use the appropriate path in the steps below!

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Round Up Your Files 🤠

We use filename patterns to separate feeder data from drinker data:

```{r list-files}
# Find all feeder files (VR*.DAT)
fileNames.f <- list.files(
  path       = extdata_path,     # 🐄 Where to look
  pattern    = "^VR.*\\.DAT$",   # 🐄 Pattern to match
  recursive  = TRUE,             # Look in subfolders too
  full.names = TRUE              # Include full path
) |> sort()                      # Keep them in order

# Find all drinker files (VW*.DAT)
fileNames.w <- list.files(
  path       = extdata_path,     # 🚰 Where to look
  pattern    = "^VW.*\\.DAT$",   # 🚰 Pattern to match
  recursive  = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
) |> sort()
```

> **Ollie's Tip:** 💡 Using different filenames? Just change the `pattern`! For example, if your files are named `FEED_20250715.csv`, you could use `pattern = "^FEED_.*\\.csv$"`.

> ⚠️ **Important File Naming Rules:**
>
> All your filenames must include the date as six digits (YYMMDD) somewhere in the name. My code finds the first six-digit sequence and treats it as the date!
>
> ✅ These work great:
>
> \- `VR200306.DAT`
>
> \- `Feeder_data_200306.DAT`
>
> \- `wat_200306_01.DAT`
>
> ❌ This won't work:
>
> \- `wat_01_200306.DAT` (because "01" appears before the date)
>
> For easiest results, name your files like mine: - Feeder data: `VRYYMMDD.DAT` - Water data: `VWYYMMDD.DAT`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Handle Daylight Saving Time ⏰

Daylight saving time changes can mess up our timestamps! Let's identify when those pesky clock changes happened:

```{r}
# Find the DST change dates for your data years
# 👉 IMPORTANT: Change these values to match your study period!
dst_df <- get_dst_switch_info(
  years = c(2020, 2021),     # 📅 EDIT THIS to match your data years!
  tz = "America/Chicago"     # EDIT THIS to your timezone if needed
                             # `Sys.timezone()` uses the timezone your computer is located at. 
)
print(dst_df)
```

> **Ollie's Note:** 🌎 This currently works for North American time zones. Using data from elsewhere? Reach out to the package maintainer - we'd love to help add support for your region!

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Process Your Data 🔄

### Keep only matching days

If you want to analyze only days with both feeder AND drinker data:

```{r}
# Match up feeder and drinker files by date
date_compare <- compare_files(fileNames.f, fileNames.w)
fileNames.f <- date_compare$feed    # Updated feeder file list
fileNames.w <- date_compare$water   # Updated drinker file list
cat("Filenames for your feeder data: \n\n", fileNames.f)
cat("\n\n")
cat("Filenames for your drinker data: \n\n", fileNames.w)

# Get the overall date range of your dataset
date_result <- get_date_range(fileNames.f)
cat("\n\n")
cat("Date range of your dataset: ", date_result)
```

### Process feeder data

Now let's clean up all those feeder logs!

```{r}
# 🔄 CHANGE THESE VALUES to match your data format! 🔄

# Define your column names (if your files don't have headers)
# 👉 EDIT THIS to match your data file structure
col_names <- c("transponder", "cow", "bin", "start", "end", "duration", 
              "startweight", "endweight", "comment", "intake", "intake2", 
              "X1", "X2", "X3", "X4", "x5")

# IDs to remove (test tags, etc.)
# 👉 EDIT THIS to remove any test tags or invalid IDs in your data
drop_ids <- c(0, 1556, 5015, 1111, 1112, 1113, 1114)

# Which feeding bins are part of your study?
# 👉 EDIT THIS to include only the bin numbers you want to analyze
bins = 1:30  # This keeps bins 1 through 30 - adjust as needed!

# Which columns do you want to keep?
# 👉 EDIT THIS to keep only the columns you need for analysis
select_cols <- c("transponder", "cow", "bin", "start", "end", 
                "duration", "startweight", "endweight", "intake")

# Process all feeder files!
all_fed <- process_all_feed(
    files = fileNames.f,
    col_names   = col_names,     # Column names for your data
    id_col      = "cow",         # 👉 EDIT if your ID column has a different name
    drop_ids    = drop_ids,      # IDs to remove
    trans_col   = "transponder", # 👉 EDIT if your transponder column has a different name
    start_col   = "start",       # 👉 EDIT if your start time column has a different name
    end_col     = "end",         # 👉 EDIT if your end time column has a different name
    drop_trans  = NULL,          # 👉 Add transponder IDs to remove if needed
    bin_col     = "bin",         # 👉 EDIT if your bin column has a different name
    bins        = bins,          # Bins to include (from above)
    select_cols = select_cols,   # Columns to keep (from above)
    sep         = ",",           # 👉 EDIT if your files use a different separator (tab="\t")
    header      = FALSE,         # 👉 Change to TRUE if your files have header rows
    daylight_change_duration = 60, # DST time shift (usually 60 minutes)
    tz          = "America/Vancouver", # 👉 EDIT to your timezone!
    adjust_dst  = TRUE           # Set to FALSE if you don't want DST corrections
)

print(str(all_fed))
```

You can now directly inspect the `all_fed` dataset, as it's lazy-loaded with the package (it won't consume memory until you actually use it).

### Process water data

And now for the drinker logs:

```{r}
# 🔄 CHANGE THESE VALUES for your water/drinker data! 🔄

# Column names for water data
# 👉 EDIT THIS if your water data has different columns
col_names_wat <- c("transponder", "cow", "bin", "start", "end", 
                  "duration", "startweight", "endweight", "intake")

# Which water bins to include
# 👉 EDIT THIS to match the drinker bin numbers at your facility
bins_water = 1:5  # This includes drinker bins 1-5

# Columns to keep
# 👉 EDIT THIS to keep only the columns you need
select_cols_wat <- c("transponder", "cow", "bin", "start", "end", 
                    "duration", "startweight", "endweight", "intake")

# Process all water files!
all_wat <- process_all_water(
    files = fileNames.w,
    col_names   = col_names_wat, # Column names from above
    id_col      = "cow",         # 👉 EDIT if your ID column has a different name
    drop_ids    = drop_ids,      # IDs to remove (using same list as feeder data)
    trans_col   = "transponder", # 👉 EDIT if your transponder column has a different name
    start_col   = "start",       # 👉 EDIT if your start time column has a different name
    end_col     = "end",         # 👉 EDIT if your end time column has a different name
    drop_trans  = NULL,          # 👉 Add transponder IDs to remove if needed
    bin_col     = "bin",         # 👉 EDIT if your bin column has a different name
    bins        = bins_water,    # Bins to include (from above)
    select_cols = select_cols_wat, # Columns to keep (from above)
    bin_offset  = 100,           # 👉 EDIT if you want a different offset for water bin IDs
                                 # This helps distinguish water bins from feed bins
    sep         = ",",           # 👉 EDIT if your files use a different separator
    header      = FALSE,         # 👉 Change to TRUE if your files have header rows
    daylight_change_duration = 60, # DST time shift
    tz          = "America/Vancouver", # 👉 EDIT to match your timezone!
    adjust_dst  = TRUE           # Set to FALSE if you don't want DST corrections
)

print(str(all_wat))
```

You can now directly inspect the `all_wat` dataset, as it's lazy-loaded with the package (it won't consume memory until you actually use it).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

You've now got clean, organized feeding and drinking data ready for analysis! Ollie is proud of you!
